page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-120g-32vram is a dedicated server instance configured with an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system provides 12 dedicated vCPUs spread over 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 120.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 10.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally provisioned via a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. While classified under the Dedicated Metal GPU family, this specific configuration reports zero operational GPUs.

Benchmark results show balanced mid-range compute and memory performance. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,742.0 alongside a single-core score of 1,477.0, with a PassMark CPU rating of 20,371.3. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 120.27 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 67.84 GB/sec. The CPU architecture includes AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI) alongside AES and FMA support, supported by a 16 MB L3 cache and 4 MB L2 cache.

Workload testing highlights notable strengths in data retrieval and caching, logging 22.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based inference handles small 135M parameter language models at 1,011.54 prompt tokens per second, but drops to 22.81 tokens per second on 7B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. With its generous memory ratio and responsive NVMe storage, this server fits memory-intensive applications such as in-memory caches, relational database systems, CI/CD compilation, and batch data processing.
